steps.message:
`client.py` is shared, not staging-only. `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` against `https://reports.example.com`, so `verify=False` in `client.py` would also disable certificate verification on the nightly production export to finance — every prod call becomes interceptable (MITM can serve any cert, and responses are trusted). The "it's just staging" premise doesn't hold for this file.

I haven't made any change yet. The options:

questions.question: client.py is shared by sync_staging.py (staging) and export_prod.py (production). How should TLS verification be handled?

options.label: Env-gated, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var (default True) that sync_staging.py sets to False. Production keeps full certificate verification; staging skips it. One small change in client.py plus one line in sync_staging.py.

options.label: Trust the staging CA instead
options.description: Point verify= at the staging CA bundle path (env var, e.g. REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE). Verification stays on everywhere; staging validates against its self-signed CA. Requires you to have the CA cert file.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: What you asked for literally: both requests calls in client.py get verify=False, which disables certificate verification for the production export as well.

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py:9-11` — `VERIFY_TLS` reads `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS`, defaulting to on. Both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py:6` — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0`, so staging skips verification for the self-signed cert.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched; production keeps full certificate verification.

`ruff format` is clean. `ruff check` reports two pre-existing `RUF100` unused-`noqa` warnings (one in each script, including the file I didn't touch) — unrelated to this change, left alone.

One note: `setdefault` means an explicitly exported `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=1` in the environment still wins over the staging script's opt-out, which is the safe direction for the failure mode. Nothing is committed.
